issues: Strength, minor: 'Highly attuned to the emotions, needs, and motivations of others' comes out as 'attuned to others' needs'; the intensifier is dropped. 'warm, responsible' (comma for 'and') pays for 'highly'.
The helping half of 'want to help others fulfill their potential' is dropped; 'finding potential in everyone' keeps only the seeing (the clause to take back under a 36-word band).
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from people, taking in patterns and possibilities, deciding by values, and liking things settled: warm, responsible, highly attuned to others' needs, finding potential in everyone, leading with inspiration.

issues: Faithfulness, minor: 'their verbal fluency' (fluent talk) becomes the manner adverb in 'often improvising fluently', which reads as improvising smoothly; 'often improvising, verbally fluent' keeps both items.

Strength, minor: 'make connections ... very quickly, and confidently proceed based on the patterns they see' comes out as 'quick to connect things and run with them'; 'very' and 'confidently' are dropped ('run with them' carries some of the confidence).

The affirmation clause ('want a lot of affirmation from others, and readily give appreciation and support') is the type's F-side signature and is dropped whole (the 36-word clause: 'seeking and giving affirmation').
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from people, taking in patterns and possibilities, deciding by values, and keeping options open: warmly enthusiastic, imaginative, quickly connecting things and running with them, often improvising, verbally fluent.
entries.strength: below: 'very quickly ... confidently proceed' rendered as 'quick to connect things and run with them'

issues: Clarity, minor: 'forceful with ideas' can be read as having forceful ideas; the source is 'forceful in presenting their ideas'. 'frank, decisive' (comma for 'and') pays for 'in presenting'.

Dropped: 'enjoy long-term planning and goal setting' and 'usually well informed, well read, ... passing it on to others'; the planning line is the type's best-known (the 36-word clause: 'planning long-term, well read').
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from people, taking in patterns and possibilities, deciding by logic, and liking things settled: frank, decisive, quick to lead, fixing inefficient procedures with systems, forceful in presenting ideas.

issues: Faithfulness: 'Loyal, follow through even in small matters' is two items (loyal; follows through even on small things); 'loyal in small matters' fuses them into a loyalty that is only about small matters, which the source does not say.

At 32 words the fix is 'loyal, reliable in small matters' ('set on harmony' for 'working hard for harmony' pays for it); the literal 'loyal, following through on small matters' is 33 words, and with 'even' restored 34 (the 36-word clause).
Dropped: 'conscientious', 'complete tasks accurately and on time', 'want to be appreciated for who they are and for what they contribute'.
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from people, taking in facts and specifics, deciding by values, and liking things settled: warmhearted, cooperative, set on harmony, loyal, reliable in small matters, tending to others' needs.

issues: Faithfulness, minor: 'bring common sense and a realistic approach to their work and make work fun' is two things; 'making work fun with common sense' makes the one the means of the other. 'sensible at work, making it fun' keeps them apart in the same six words.
'Exuberant lovers of life, people, and material comforts' loses 'material' ('comforts' alone is vaguer); 'people' is carried by the E phrase.
Dropped: 'adapt readily to new people and environments' and 'learn best by trying a new skill with other people' (the 36-word clause: 'adapting readily to new people').
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from people, taking in facts and specifics, deciding by values, and keeping options open: outgoing, friendly, accepting, exuberant about life and comforts, sensible at work, making it fun.

issues: Strength: 'have a clear set of logical standards, systematically follow them and want others to also' comes out as 'holding everyone to clear standards'; a wish that others follow becomes enforcement, a shade above the source. 'following clear standards and expecting the same' sits at it ('organizing projects and people efficiently' pays for the two words; 'results' goes).

Dropped: 'forceful in implementing their plans', which the source gives ESTJ and ENTJ alike and the drafts keep only for ENTJ (the 36-word clause: 'forceful in implementing plans'); also 'take care of routine details'.
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from people, taking in facts and specifics, deciding by logic, and liking things settled: practical, matter-of-fact, organizing projects and people efficiently, following clear standards and expecting the same.
entries.strength: above: 'want others to also' rendered as 'holding everyone to'

issues: Faithfulness, minor: 'want to act energetically to solve the problem' and 'focus on the here and now' merge into 'energetic in the here and now', losing the problem-solving action that separates this portrait from ESFP's; 'energetically tackling the problem at hand' keeps both in six words.
Dropped: 'take a pragmatic approach focused on immediate results' (only partly carried by the S phrase) and 'enjoy material comforts and style' (the 36-word clause: 'wanting immediate results').
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from people, taking in facts and specifics, deciding by logic, and keeping options open: flexible, tolerant, bored by theory, energetically tackling the problem at hand, learning by doing.

issues: Faithfulness: 'develop a clear vision about how best to serve the common good' comes out as 'serving the common good'; the vision is the type's defining element, and without it the clause reads as plain humanitarian.
'Want to understand what motivates people and are insightful about others' keeps only its second half ('insightful about people').
At 32 words the best I find is 'envisioning the common good' (the suggested edit); the clause whole needs the 36-word band: 'pursuing a clear vision of the common good' for 'serving the common good'.
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from reflection, taking in patterns and possibilities, deciding by values, and liking things settled: seeking meaning and connection, insightful about people, holding firm values, envisioning the common good.

issues: Strength, minor: 'high standards of competence and performance, for themselves and others' comes out as 'expecting competence of oneself and others'; 'high standards' is the stronger claim. 'holding oneself and others to high standards' sits at it ('driven to realize ideas', without 'one's', pays for the word).

Dropped: 'quickly see patterns in external events and develop long-range explanatory perspectives' (the N phrase carries patterns, not the long range; the 36-word clause: 'seeing long-range patterns'), 'when committed, organize a job and carry it through' (J phrase), 'achieving their goals'.

issues: Strength, minor: 'logical explanations for everything that interests them' comes out as 'for everything'; the scope qualifier is dropped and the claim widens. 'logically explaining whatever interests one' restores it in five words (the verb shifts from seeking to doing; Roger's call which matters more).

'Skeptical, sometimes critical, always analytical' is quoted whole (five words); the standards rule says paraphrase, not quote. I would keep it, since rewording would disturb the hedge, but Roger should know; the same holds for INFP's 'accepting unless a value is threatened'.

Dropped: 'unusual ability to focus in depth to solve problems in their area of interest', the type's most distinctive line (the 36-word clause: 'focusing deeply on problems'); also 'logic' twice with the T phrase.
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from reflection, taking in patterns and possibilities, deciding by logic, and keeping options open: logically explaining whatever interests one, preferring ideas to company, skeptical, sometimes critical, always analytical.

issues: Faithfulness: the source's whole second sentence ('analyze what makes things work and readily get through large amounts of data to isolate the core of practical problems') is dropped; it is the type's hallmark, and what remains (tolerant, flexible, observant, quick fixer) is the thinnest portrait in the set.

At 32 words the clause fits only by dropping 'flexible', which the P phrase carries (the writer's own practice for ESFP), and 'quickly fixing it' for 'then quick with a workable fix'; at 36 it comes back whole: 'tolerant, flexible, quietly observing until a problem appears, then quick to fix it, analyzing what makes things work'.
'Workable solutions' as 'a workable fix' is fine in voice.
entries.suggested_edit: This means drawing energy from reflection, taking in facts and specifics, deciding by logic, and keeping options open: tolerant, quietly observing until a problem appears, quickly fixing it, analyzing how things work.

sets.name: MBTI 4-cube (the sixteen types)
sets.review: SHAPE AND GRAIN. Agree with the writer: one template throughout, preferences first (18 words, fixed phrasing, two phrases per dichotomy) and portrait second (14 words), every entry exactly 32 words and one sentence, every description carrying the four phrases its code calls for (checked by script, as were the absence of type codes, letters, preference names and the instrument's name). Adjacent corners of the cube differ in exactly one phrase, so each dichotomy is one word swap read off the set. The portraits are at one grain, lists of four to seven adjectives and participles; the I-S four and ESFJ are the most list-like (ISFJ runs to seven bare items), the N types more clause-like, which is the texture of the Foundation's own paragraphs. No member is at a different grain from the others. DICHOTOMIES. Readable off the set from the preamble alone. The portraits are not controlled for them and echo them unevenly: beyond the writer's ESTJ 'practical, matter-of-fact' (S) and ISTJ 'orderly in everything' (J), ESTP and ISTP 'flexible' (P), INTP 'logical explanations ... always analytical' (T), INFP 'living one's values' and 'unless a value is threatened' (F; with the preamble, 'value(s)' three times in one sentence), ENTJ 'decisive' (J). Not a fault, but the echoes mean the portrait adds less independent information than its 14 words suggest, and since the preamble is 56% of every description the sixteen description embeddings will be dominated by the shared phrases: the cube will be clean in description space by construction, which is presumably the point of the set. THE BAND. My view: relax to about 36 for this set, uniformly, so that all sixteen are again the same length. The fixed 18-word preamble leaves the portrait 14 words, half what a plain corpus trait gets for its whole content, and the clauses that went were disproportionately the hallmarks and the hedged lines ('may act as catalysts', 'usually well informed', 'can be catalysts'), so the selection sharpened the set a shade. The band is p10-p90, descriptive; four words over p90 on a set that is read beside itself costs little, and the departure can be recorded in the entries' notes. The clause that would come back per type (about four words each, on top of the 32-word fixes in the entries): ENFJ 'and helping them fulfill it'; ENFP 'seeking and giving affirmation'; ENTJ 'planning long-term, well read'; ENTP 'good at reading people'; ESFJ 'following through even on small matters' for 'reliable in small matters'; ESFP 'adapting readily to new people'; ESTJ 'forceful in implementing plans'; ESTP 'wanting immediate results'; INFJ 'pursuing a clear vision of the common good' for 'envisioning the common good'; INFP 'curious' and 'loyal to one's people'; INTJ 'seeing long-range patterns'; INTP 'focusing deeply on problems'; ISFJ 'those close to one' for 'one's people', plus 'responsible'; ISFP 'not pushing one's views' (the writer's own first candidate); ISTJ 'serious' and 'taking pleasure in order'; ISTP 'analyzing what makes things work' with 'flexible' and 'then' kept. If the band stays at 32, the restorations that matter most are ISTP, INFJ, ISFP, ENFP, ESTJ and INTP, in that order; the first two are in the entries as edits because the dropped clause is the type's defining one. STRENGTH. Agree: positive and measured as the source, and markedly milder than the corpus's plain traits in the same regions (I read dominant, controlling and detached; all three are sharper than ENTJ, ESTJ and INTP). Per entry: two sit a shade above (ESTJ 'holding everyone to', INTP 'for everything'), three a shade below (ENFJ 'attuned', ENFP 'quick ... run with them', INTJ 'expecting competence'), eleven at source; all five are fixed within the 32 words in the suggested edits. The four kept hedges (INTP 'sometimes', ENFP 'often', ENTP 'apt to', INFP 'unless') are right, and the writer is right that the other twelve read a shade firmer for lacking one. VERBATIM. INTP's closing line and INFP's 'accepting unless a value is threatened' are quoted whole; the standards rule (paraphrase, do not quote) is against it. I would keep both, since rewording would disturb the hedges, but it is Roger's call. WRITER'S DEPARTURE (a). Agree with 'deciding by values' over the packet's 'deciding by values and people': the swap against 'deciding by logic' is unambiguous, and 'people' twice in the E-F four would read badly. The cost: 'values' alone can be heard as principled rather than people-minded. NEAREST EXISTING. Every stem named exists in corpus_stems.txt; the lines are plausible, and none of the sixteen is a near-duplicate of a plain trait (each is a conjunction of four facets). One omission across all sixteen lines: the plain corpus pair closest to the J and P phrases is closure_seeking ('needing every question settled') / ambiguity_tolerant ('at ease with unsettled questions'), which no line names; organized (an orderly answer), decisive (firm recommendations), flexible (working within constraints) and spontaneous (variety in structure and tone) are weaker matches. Add it to the J and P facets of all sixteen lines. The writer is right that J does not touch judgmental (read: harsh opinions of others), and 'liking things settled' does not touch settled (read: living in one place for decades). UNVERIFIED. I did not fetch the Foundation's pages (per the brief), so the writer's statement that the four preference phrases are the Preferences page's own wording is taken on trust, as is the single-page provenance. GENERATION WATCH. The label 'ENFJ (MBTI)' is injected as the trait name, so the generator will likely write 'you are an ENFJ' into the instructions; rule 6's leak check applies to the type code as much as to the instrument name, and self-labelling is the one register that propagates for traits. WORDINGS TO GLANCE AT in the ok entries: ISFJ 'one's people' (idiom for one's close circle, but readable as staff or kin), ENFP 'run with them', ISTP 'fix'.

summary:
Sixteen drafts, all in form (32 words, one sentence, 'This means', the four phrases per code present, no type code, letters or preference names, US spelling; checked by script), all from the Foundation's one page, all at or within a shade of the source's strength.
Five ok (ENTP, INFP, ISFJ, ISFP, ISTJ); eleven edit, of which four are substantive (ESFJ 'loyal in small matters' reads two items as one; ESFP fuses common sense and making work fun; INFJ drops the clear vision; ISTP drops the analyze-what-makes-things-work sentence) and seven are one- or two-word strength or clarity fixes; every edit has a 32-word replacement in the file.
Set: one grain and shape, the four dichotomies readable off the preamble; I agree with the writer's set_review and would relax the band to about 36 for all sixteen, so each portrait takes back its hallmark clause (listed per type in the set review; ISTP, INFJ, ISFP, ENFP, ESTJ, INTP matter most if the band stays).
Nearest-existing lines are plausible but all sixteen should add closure_seeking / ambiguity_tolerant for the J and P facets; INTP and INFP each quote a five-word line verbatim, which Roger should rule on; watch the generator for 'you are an ENFJ' self-labelling.
